Source: Penn CIS610 2018 lecture slides, Chapter15 Proposition15.7, printedp777 / PDFpage10.
Mathematical transcription: A local isometry pi:M->N from a complete nonempty Riemannian manifold M to connected Riemannian N is a Riemannian covering map; in particular it is surjective.
Source statement does not assume source connectedness. Same lecture series Chapter7 printedp340 / PDFpage9 explicitly states that manifolds need not be connected. Hausdorff and second countability are standing assumptions stated on printedp333 / PDFpage2.
Scope caveat: Nonemptiness is implicit in usual nonempty manifold convention or must be stated explicitly; the present Lean source-connectedness entails it, but disconnected nonempty sources remain excluded. The two-copy identity local isometry R disjoint-union R -> R is complete and covers the intended omitted class.

source.title: CIS610 Chapter15 Isometries, Local Isometries, Riemannian Coverings
source.locator: Proposition15.7 printedp777/PDF10; Chapter7 printedp340/PDF9 explicitly permits disconnected manifolds

scope_qualification: Full independent covering statement permits disconnected nonempty complete source; exact final root restricts source to ConnectedSpace N and finite MetricSpace N inducing g-distance. This is a completed but narrower scope. The finite intrinsic metric itself also restricts disconnected components, so do not claim that deleting ConnectedSpace alone repairs full scope or that two copies of R satisfy all remaining Lean hypotheses.
